questions.q: What is a sample ratio mismatch (SRM), and why check for it first?
options: The treatment group converts more than control; it proves the change works
The two groups have different variances; it invalidates the t-test
The sample is larger than the planned size; it makes the test more powerful
The observed group sizes differ from the planned split by more than chance allows; it usually signals a bug in assignment or logging
questions.explain: SRM is checked with a chi-square goodness-of-fit test on group counts. A failing check means the data pipeline or randomization is suspect, so outcome results cannot be trusted yet.

questions.q: Control converted at 10.775% and treatment at 12.25%, each with 4,000 users, giving a two-sided p-value of 0.0388. What does this p-value mean?
options: If the true rates were equal, a gap at least this large would occur by chance about 3.9% of the time
There is a 96.1% probability that treatment is better
The lift is 3.88 percentage points
The treatment is worth shipping
questions.explain: A p-value is the probability of data at least this extreme if the null hypothesis were true. It is not the probability that treatment is better and says nothing about the size or value of the lift.

questions.q: For a 2x2 table of group by converted, how does the chi-square test of independence (no continuity correction) relate to the pooled two-proportion z-test?
options: The chi-square statistic equals z squared and gives the same two-sided p-value
They usually disagree, so you must run both
The chi-square test only works for more than two groups
The z-test is one-sided and the chi-square test is two-sided, so they cannot be compared
questions.explain: For a 2x2 table without continuity correction, chi-square equals z squared, so the p-values match. In the lesson, 2.067 squared is 4.27.

questions.q: The 95% confidence interval for the lift is 0.08 to 2.87 percentage points. What is the best reading?
options: The lift is exactly 1.5 points
The lift is almost certainly at least 2 points
The lift is probably positive, but it could plausibly be very small or nearly double the point estimate
The interval proves the lift is practically important
questions.explain: The interval shows the plausible range of the true lift. Because it is wide, the decision should weigh both the small and large ends against cost.

questions.q: Revenue per user is 7.11 in treatment versus 6.59 in control, with a Welch t-test p-value of 0.33. What should you conclude?
options: Treatment definitely increases revenue by $0.52 per user
Treatment decreases revenue
The difference is well within what noise could produce, so you cannot claim a revenue effect
The t-test is invalid and should be replaced by a z-test
questions.explain: A p-value of 0.33 means the observed gap is easily explained by chance. The test was also not designed for revenue, so its power may be limited.
